outline.description: Sets out the executive actions affecting the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP), the plaintiffs’ claims, district court rulings, and the Ninth Circuit’s sequence of stays leading to this interim order.
subtopics: Executive Order 14163 (Jan. 20, 2025): suspension of refugee entry under 8 U.S.C. §§ 1182(f), 1185(a)
Executive Order 14169 and State Department’s suspension of USRAP funding
Parties: refugees (admitted and approved but abroad) and three resettlement organizations with State Department cooperative agreements
Claims: Refugee Act violations (Refugee Act of 1980) and APA challenges to funding suspensions and contract terminations
District court preliminary injunctions (Feb. 28 and Mar. 24, 2025): enjoining EO provisions and funding suspensions; ordering reinstatement of cooperative agreements
Government appeals and Ninth Circuit initial stay orders (Mar. 25 with carveout; Apr. 21 and May 9 clarifications)
District court’s July 14 enforcement framework and magistrate appointment; government’s July 17 emergency motion; Ninth Circuit administrative stay on July 18
Current order: vacates prior stays, denies emergency motion as moot, and issues a new stay pending appeal with a limited exception

outline.description: Explains the standards and statutes central to the order: stay factors, presidential entry-suspension authority, and statutory/APA constraints on refugee resettlement services.
subtopics: Stay pending appeal factors under Nken v. Holder: likelihood of success, irreparable injury, injury to others, public interest; primacy of first two factors
Presidential authority under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) and Trump v. Hawaii’s deferential review
Refugee Act provisions on post-admission services: 8 U.S.C. § 1522(a)(1)(A), (b)(1)(A)(ii), (d)(2)(B), (e)(7)(A); implementing regulations at 45 C.F.R. §§ 400.200 et seq.
Funding and appropriations context: FY 2025 appropriations and rescissions; § 1523 reporting requirement
APA oversight of agency action: challenges to suspension of funding and termination of cooperative agreements

outline.description: Details how the panel applies Nken, distinguishing between the EO’s suspension of refugee entry and the cessation of resettlement services and agreements.
subtopics: Likelihood of success: strong for the government on EO 14163 entry suspension under § 1182(f) with limited judicial scrutiny per Hawaii
Likelihood of success: not strong for the government on at least one APA challenge tied to statutory duties under § 1522 to provide reception and placement services to admitted refugees
Irreparable harm and public interest: weight of national interests and foreign affairs for entry suspension; domestic statutory obligations for services to admitted refugees
Balance of equities: preserving presidential discretion on entry while preventing unlawful cessation of mandated services

outline.description: Clarifies exactly what the court stays, what it allows to proceed, and the immediate operational steps it orders the government to take.
subtopics: Vacatur of prior Ninth Circuit administrative and partial stays (July 18; Mar. 25 as amended)
Stay of district court’s Feb. 28 and Mar. 24 preliminary injunctions in their entirety except as specified
Directed exception: government must reinstate cooperative agreements necessary to provide usual and customary § 1522 reception and placement services for refugees already admitted
Scope: services include employment training, English language training, cash assistance design consistent with statute, and case management; special provisions for unaccompanied minors when necessary
Government’s prior representation about preparing new RFPs and the court’s concern over lack of progress
Denial of the government’s July 17 emergency motion as moot
Opinion on the merits to follow; stay remains pending final resolution of the appeal

outline.chapter_title: Separate Opinion and Doctrinal Dispute Over § 1522
outline.description: Summarizes Judge Lee’s partial concurrence/dissent and frames the statutory interpretation debate that will shape the merits.
subtopics: Agreement: President’s broad § 1182(f) authority supports staying the district court’s injunction on entry suspension
Disagreement: whether § 1522 mandates provision of services versus merely authorizes them

Textual cues emphasized by dissent: § 1522 title (“Authorization”), repeated “is authorized” language in §§ 1522(b)-(e), and conditional phrasing in §§ 1522(d)(2)(B) and (e)(7)(A) (“if necessary,” “as needed”)
Majority’s contrary indicators: mandatory “shall” in § 1522(a)(1)(A) tied to providing assistance to admitted refugees, statutory/regulatory structure, and appropriations context
Implications for APA review: whether terminating funding and cooperative agreements conflicts with a statutory mandate or falls within executive discretion
Significance for future merits opinion: contours of statutory duty, agency discretion, and judicial remedies
